title: E002: a plain fn, including main, cannot directly read a module source/derived.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Track ordinary reads dynamically when a derivation is active; otherwise read the current value. Keep explicit snapshots for deliberately untracked reads. Cost: implicit context sensitivity and effect inference.

title: E003: a derived binding cannot be assigned.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep ordinary derived bindings read-only; an explicit writable lens could route writes to sources without changing this rule.

title: Claimed E008: derived computations cannot loop, including through callees.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Document pure loops as supported, retaining effect checks. Optional evaluation fuel addresses nontermination; recursion already has the same problem. Cost: documentation and, if desired, a fuel counter.

title: Claimed E008: control flow reached through a derived callee.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Define purity by effects, not return/if syntax; retain lexical return targets. Cost: clarify the contract; these examples already pass.

title: E008: derived values cannot use snap, even through a helper.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep the ban on genuinely untracked reactive inputs to a derivation. A separate frozen-at-construction value could be explicit input, rather than a hidden read.

title: E008: derived values cannot reach an act fn, including through a plain wrapper.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Permit an action proven to read no reactive state and have no effects, or add effect-polymorphic function types. Cost: interprocedural summaries; do not simply allow untracked reads.

title: E008: even an effect-free, literal-returning act fn is forbidden in const.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Accept callees proved pure and independent of reactive state, regardless of act annotation. Cost: effect summaries and less annotation-based predictability.

title: E008: a track fn cannot reach an act fn, even if never called by a derived value.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep a tracked/pure signature by default, allow proven effect-free callees or context-sensitive checking. Cost: effect typing and possibly errors at use sites.

title: E008: an extern fn cannot be reached from derived, const, or track fn.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Add a host-validated pure extern contract, forbidding reactive reads/writes and nondeterminism. Cost: a trusted host boundary, like other FFI promises.

title: E010: cyclic equations in the reactive graph are rejected.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep rejection for ordinary derived values. A separate delayed stream/fixed-point feature would need different semantics and convergence rules.

title: E010 also rejects a cycle in an unreachable if branch.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Constant-fold branches before cycle analysis; more general dynamic cycles can be checked during evaluation. Cost: optimization-aware diagnostics or runtime errors instead of an unconditional static guarantee.

title: E017: derived evaluation cannot print or perform I/O through a callee.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep the transitive effect prohibition. Put effects in watches/handlers, and feed external input into sources.

title: E017: a derived computation cannot emit an event.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep emit outside derived evaluation. No implicit deferred-event escape is compatible with ordinary pure equations.

title: E017: const initializers must be pure, although they run once at startup.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Keep pure const; teach the existing one-shot source initializer (let with no reactive reads) for effectful configuration. Cost: clearer startup-order documentation; an explicit init spelling could improve discoverability.

title: E008: const cannot read reactive state, even an immutable module let.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Allow immutable-source constants proven independent of mutable state, or a named startup snapshot form. Cost: constant propagation / a separate snapshot contract.

title: E017 conservatively rejects passing an effectful function to a callee that never calls it.
section: Reactive reads, purity, and graph structure
relax: Summarize which callback parameters a function invokes; permit unused/stored callbacks. Cost: higher-order effect analysis, especially for escaping values.

title: E011: watch cannot be declared inside an ordinary function.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Allow scoped watches returning a disposable handle, or sugar for a live fn instance. Cost: lifecycle API and dynamic registration order.

title: E011: event handlers cannot be declared inside a function.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Allow scoped subscriptions with explicit ownership and disposal, and deterministic creation order. Cost: dynamic handler lifetime rules.

title: Reactive declarations are not local function variables; local derived syntax is unavailable.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Permit an explicit scoped reactive declaration with ownership, or direct users to live fn. Cost: scoped graph nodes; add a targeted error now.

title: The same let spelling is a reactive source/derived at module level and an ordinary snapshot local inside fn.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Add explicit source/derived forms and a migration path for plain module constants; retain inference as optional sugar. Cost: compatibility and one extra concept.

title: A bare top-level assignment is a parse error, although top-level if may assign during initialization.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Allow initialization statements in declaration order, settling at the documented module boundary. Cost: grammar and initialization ordering tests.

title: E016: a module let without mut cannot be reassigned.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep explicit mutability for ordinary bindings.

title: E009: an immutable local cannot be assigned.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep; declare let mut for a changing local.

title: E009: const cannot be assigned.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep const immutable; improve the diagnostic to distinguish a constant from a local.

title: E027: fn main or another plain fn cannot directly change a source; write act fn.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Infer source-writing functions as actions, still forbid them from derived contexts, and expose their effect in tooling/signatures. Cost: less explicit batch boundaries and effect inference.

title: E027: track fn cannot directly change a source.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep a pure tracked-computation role; move the transition into act fn/on. Renaming a track fn is appropriate only when its callers also permit an action.

title: E027: an impl method cannot directly write a module source, and cannot be declared act fn.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Allow act methods, with the same source ownership and batching checks as act fn. Cost: method effect signatures and dispatch plumbing.

title: E028 is a WARNING: a watch is allowed to write its own module source.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep a warning for redundant derived-state synchronization; allow intentional effect writes. Explain ordering and require an explicit action for larger transitions. Cost: no additional graph guarantee from simply moving the write into emit.

title: E029 warns about watch feedback; watches run at most once per batch.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep the warning; optionally provide an explicit next-batch event queue or bounded fixed-point mode. Cost: new timing/convergence semantics. Moving the same feedback to an on handler does not by itself break the cycle.

title: E030 warns when a functional collection result is dropped.
section: State writes, watches, and declaration placement
relax: Keep the warning, suggest let ys=push(xs,2) for immutable inputs or let mut plus xs.push(2). Cost: context-aware fixes.

title: E032: an importing module cannot write another module's public mutable source.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Retain read-only exports by default; optional explicit exported setter/capability could authorize batched writes. Cost: a capability/visibility surface and weaker owner encapsulation.

title: E033: other modules cannot name private struct fields, including literals, with, writes, and patterns.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep default field privacy and explicit pub; no need to relax to reduce reactive friction.

title: E034: unavailable target modules/functions cannot be used (probe: fs on web).
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Allow an explicit host capability adapter. Cost: asynchronous/browser semantics and a real web runtime; keep E034 without such an adapter.

title: E035 warns that a local file with a library module name cannot be imported using that name.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Add an explicit local/package-qualified import namespace. Cost: one resolution form; retain the warning for ambiguous old imports.

title: E031: a generic call must satisfy its declared trait bounds.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep bounds checked at calls; improve missing-trait guidance to distinguish removable bounds from implementable traits.

title: E021: ? needs a declared Result/Option return type and a matching operand kind.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Infer a consistent Result/Option return when unambiguous; retain kind checking and use explicit match for conversion. Cost: bidirectional return inference and ambiguity diagnostics.

title: E021: Result ? requires exactly the enclosing Result error type; no conversion.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Add explicit map_error or a declared conversion trait analogous to Rust From; never guess a conversion. Cost: trait/conversion coherence and extra typing rules.

title: E025: a recursive type with no finite value is rejected.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Allow an explicitly uninhabited declaration while rejecting recursive construction; never silently build infinite eager values. Cost: exhaustiveness and representation support.

title: E012: direct file imports cannot escape the project root.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Allow explicit configured import roots; keep dependency declarations preferred. Cost: reproducibility and tooling configuration.

title: E013: cyclic module imports are rejected.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Permit pure/type-only strongly connected components, reject cycles involving initialization state. Cost: staged module resolution and SCC analysis.

title: E022: a non-pub module item cannot be imported.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep export privacy; correct the spec code cross-reference.

title: E014/E001/E007: names, imports, and types must resolve in the current module.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep lexical/module resolution; add likely-import suggestions where known.

title: E004: a scope cannot define the same item twice.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep duplicate binding/parameter rejection; local shadowing remains a separate rule.

title: E024: a type alias cannot recursively expand to itself.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep aliases finite; use a nominal recursive type.

title: E023: a value without a function type cannot be called.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep; an explicit callable trait would be a separate language feature.

title: E019: a method must exist for the receiver type.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep method resolution; mention both inherent and trait impl fixes.

title: E020: trait impl signatures must match the declared trait.
section: Modules, visibility, targets, and ordinary static checking
relax: Keep trait signature checking.

title: A live fn parameter cannot be declared mut.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Desugar mut parameters into per-instance source members, or explain using let mut n=x. Cost: clarify visibility and tracking of parameter reads.

title: Claimed rule: component parameters stay fixed for the instance lifetime.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Enforce assignment rejection for fixed parameters, or explicitly promote mutable parameters to reactive source members. The former needs no new semantics.

title: A component member cannot use a destructuring pattern.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Lower member destructuring to hidden members/projections, evaluate the initializer once. Cost: names, spans, and projection dependencies.

title: A component member function cannot have type parameters.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Specialize member functions by instance-template and type arguments. Cost: code generation/cache keys, not a reactive semantic concession.

title: A component member function cannot have mut parameters or mut self.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Allow ordinary mut arguments with normal write-back rules; retain no mut self until handle semantics are specified. Cost: lowering and effect propagation.

title: E008: derived/const/track fn cannot construct an instance.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep allocation/subscription creation out of pure computations. Reconciliation/keyed construction would be an explicit owned effect feature.

title: A module let whose initializer constructs a component runs once, even when arguments are reactive.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Add explicit construction/snapshot syntax or a compiler hover showing startup-only inputs; live parameters could instead be explicit reactive inputs. Cost: another binding mode/API.

title: E032: code outside an instance cannot directly change its public source member.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Support explicitly exported write capabilities/setters; keep read-only public handles by default. Cost: expanded API authority. Report E032 before irrelevant receiver-mutability advice.

title: E033: non-pub component members are inaccessible even elsewhere in the same file.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep component privacy; use an instance-specific diagnostic instead of module wording.

title: Component functions/events cannot be read as first-class values.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Introduce bound member closures/event handles carrying instance ownership and effects. Cost: lifetime and effect analysis; a lambda calling the member is a limited workaround.

title: A targetless watch cannot read an instance member.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Track instance-member reads dynamically in targetless watches, or accept an expression target. Cost: subscriptions must switch/dispose as handles change.

title: emit requires a name chain; an indexed instance must be bound first.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Accept any once-evaluated instance expression as an emit receiver. Cost: expression lowering and preserving evaluation order.

title: E010: a component template cannot have cyclic bare-member derived equations.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep, with any future delayed/fixed-point graphs explicitly separate.

title: The component/module template dependency graph must also be acyclic.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Retain rejection of an actual value cycle; conservative type/template-level cycles could be allowed with per-instance runtime cycle checks. Cost: later errors and dynamic graph validation.

title: A derived value may not come to depend on itself through dynamic instance reads.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep the runtime cycle guard; improve the trace with the instance dependency path.

title: An instance may not hold itself, even when no reactive dependency cycle exists.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Provide weak instance links, or a cycle collector/owner-arena with explicit disposal. Cost: weak-link handling or collection overhead and disposal scheduling. The book should teach the retention mechanism.

title: An instance may not read a module binding before its initial value is set.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep the guard; possible future two-phase initialization may defer some member evaluation without exposing unset values.

title: E030 warns when a constructed instance is immediately discarded.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep this warning and handle-based lifetime rule; scoped explicit ownership is preferable to invisible permanent registration.

title: Copying an instance handle aliases identity; it does not copy the state.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Keep handle identity; offer explicit clone-state construction if desired. Fix module alias receiver unwrapping. Cost: an explicit cloning API, not implicit duplicated subscriptions.

title: A live fn body cannot declare types, nested components, imports, or const members.
section: Components and handle semantics
relax: Allow lexically scoped types/constants where their lifetime is clear; hoist template-independent items. Cost: scoping and export resolution.

title: Explicit type arguments at generic call sites are not supported.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Add explicit generic call/type-constructor arguments, reusing existing monomorphization. Cost: grammar disambiguation and diagnostics.

title: A generic call with unconstrained type arguments is rejected; bare generic type names also need all arguments.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep unresolved types an error; add the explicit argument escape hatch above rather than arbitrary default types.

title: A tuple enum variant has exactly one payload value; Node(Tree,Tree) is rejected.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Desugar multi-payload variants to one tuple payload; preserve pattern arity in syntax. Cost: parser/pattern sugar and compatibility decisions for display.

title: An if used as an operand has no direct else if chain.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Share if grammar in expression and statement positions. Cost: parser/AST normalization; preserve existing branch value/effect checking.

title: Operand-if branches cannot contain statements, unlike a function-tail if.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Use value blocks in both positions; apply context-sensitive purity checks to effects. Cost: one coherent block AST instead of separate forms.

title: Match arm blocks in derived/watch/on contexts cannot contain loops/control-flow, emit, or module assignments.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Allow full arm blocks in effect contexts, keep derived purity checks, and preserve return/break lexical scopes. Cost: uniform lowering of match bodies.

title: map_new needs an import, while map methods such as m.len do not.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Suggest import collections { map_new }; optionally add Map::new(). Cost: symbol-to-import lookup or one type-function alias.

title: There is no empty map literal ({} is not a Map initializer).
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Add a typed empty map literal or Map::new(). Cost: grammar/context disambiguation; no graph cost.

title: Map keys are only integers, String, Bool, or Char; not tuples, structs, or floats.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Support structurally ordered tuple/enum/struct keys, and optional explicit total float keys. Cost: comparison definitions and compatible display/iteration order.

title: An unannotated empty-array binding cannot infer its element type.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep ambiguity rejection or infer from later uses where sound. Cost of the latter: delayed local inference.

title: An unconstrained closure parameter defaults to Int, so field reads need context or an annotation.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Delay inference until uses, or report an unknown parameter type rather than guessing Int. Cost: broader constraint solving and potential compatibility changes.

title: Closures capture locals by value and cannot assign a captured mutable local.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Offer explicit mutable captures with closure state or reference-cell types; retain value capture by default. Cost: callable mutability/lifetime and effect rules.

title: return is forbidden in a closure body, including its match arms.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Permit return to the nearest closure/function boundary. Cost: control-flow lowering; continue rejecting jumps across closure boundaries.

title: Functions and values containing functions have no ==, !=, or contains comparison.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep no extensional equality; optionally expose explicit function identity, never silently equate functions by behavior. Cost: stable closure identity and clarified graph change detection.

title: Functions and any containing value cannot be printed/interpolated/to_string.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Give functions a non-executable opaque debug display and recursively display containers. Cost: formatting stability; do not expose addresses as portable identities.

title: A call with mut arguments must be a statement or a let initializer, not a larger expression.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Sequence call, write-back, then surrounding expression; preserve evaluate-once places and failure atomicity. Cost: temporary values and ordering specification.

title: Each mut parameter requires explicit mut on a mutable-place argument.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Retain writable-place checking; optional inference of call-site mut with tooling indication. Cost: mutation becomes less visually explicit.

title: Functions with mut parameters cannot be stored or passed as function values.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Add first-class mut-parameter function types, or require an explicit adapter closure. Cost: indirect call ABI/place validation and effect-aware typing.

title: A mut self method must be a standalone place call and cannot return a value.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Allow results and expression calls after copy-back. Cost: the same sequencing representation already needed by mut functions.

title: A method with its own type parameters cannot have mut self.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Specialize before applying ordinary mut-self lowering. Cost: combining two existing compiler paths.

title: Methods cannot have mut parameters other than mut self.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Apply the free-function mut ABI to methods, with evaluate-once receiver/arguments. Cost: lowering and alias/write-back ordering rules.

title: A generic type cannot have an impl specialized to one concrete argument.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Allow disjoint concrete impls, reject overlapping methods unless precedence is explicit. Cost: coherence/overlap checking.

title: Built-in Eq and Ord cannot be implemented for a user type.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep graph change equality structural by default; add explicit ordering/comparison traits or structural Ord for eligible types. Cost: law/coherence policy; do not let arbitrary effectful equality control settling.

title: Tuples have two or more values; (x,) is forbidden.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Accept one-element tuples with trailing comma. Cost: type/display/pattern support for arity one.

title: Unit is a type/block result, but the obvious () expression is rejected.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Add the () literal. Cost: parser and constant representation already present in IR.

title: Float literal patterns are rejected, even with a catch-all.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Allow literal patterns with IEEE equality, warn for NaN/nonexact comparisons, or teach guarded matches. Cost: matching policy; no exhaustiveness credit for float literals.

title: A match must be exhaustive; numeric/string literal arms need a catch-all, guarded arms do not prove coverage.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep exhaustiveness. Better finite missing-case examples would improve diagnostics without weakening it.

title: Branch/return types must agree without implicit numeric widening in annotated functions.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Allow only lossless, explicit or expected-type-directed numeric literal conversions; keep incompatible branches rejected. Cost: conversion rules and clearer inferred-type reporting.

title: Arrays must have a single element type.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep homogeneous arrays; model alternatives with enums.

title: A final semicolon does not discard a block value as it does in Rust.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Either keep and teach the difference clearly, or add explicit discard expression syntax. Cost of Rust-style semicolons: a breaking grammar/value change.

title: break/continue require a loop in the same function; they cannot cross closure boundaries.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep lexical loop boundaries.

title: Bitwise compound assignment forms such as &= are absent.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Desugar bit compound assignment using the existing evaluate-once place machinery. Cost: parser/operator coverage.

title: Identifiers/code outside strings/comments are ASCII-only.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Support normalized Unicode XID identifiers with optional confusable lint. Cost: normalization/versioned identifier policy.

title: A line starting with binary minus is rejected instead of continuing the prior expression.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep for now; a newline-sensitive expression grammar could accept standalone unary minus. Cost: clear continuation/statement boundary rules and possible compatibility changes.

title: Only documented escapes are valid; bare {} is not a formatting placeholder.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep unknown-escape errors; add useful explicit Unicode/hex escapes if needed, plus a targeted empty-interpolation repair. Cost: lexical support.

title: Claimed rule: names beginning __mod_ are reserved for compiler-generated names.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Use symbol identity/hygienic namespaces internally; until then consistently reject the reserved prefix with a specific diagnostic. Cost: internal name representation or complete validation.

title: E026 warns for older syntax; it does not prohibit it.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Keep migration warnings configurable and offer concrete edits; avoid reporting them as hard restrictions.

title: Library free functions cannot be used as first-class values without a wrapper closure.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Reify typed builtin function pointers/adapters, preserving their effect summaries. Cost: first-class builtin dispatch and polymorphic builtin specialization.

title: A mut-parameter function with no declared result has no bindable value, even when its body ends in an expression.
section: Generics, values, grammar, and library surface
relax: Infer a user result separately from changed arguments, or offer a targeted annotation fix. Cost: result/copy-back ABI typing; keep no-result calls unbindable while they truly return nothing.

title: main must take no parameters and return Unit or Int; Int is an exit status.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Optionally allow main(args:[String]) and Result exits with an explicit CLI mapping. Cost: ABI and exit/error policy; keep the current signature check until then.

title: extern fn parameters cannot be mut.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Return an explicit updated value or define host copy-back results. Cost: a new trusted host ABI and failure atomicity rules.

title: The CLI cannot run a program declaring any extern fn without a host implementation, even if unused.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Link only reachable extern declarations, or let the CLI load an explicit host adapter. Cost: reachability / host plugin loading.

title: Events/handlers have fixed payload arity and types; emit does not invent missing values.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Keep arity/type validation; defaulted payload arguments could be a separate explicit feature.

title: Integer literals must fit their selected width; unsuffixed integers are Int64.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Keep range checking; suggest the wider type/suffix where it fits.

title: Integer arithmetic, division by zero, casts, and shifts fail on invalid values instead of wrapping silently.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Keep checked defaults; explicit checked/wrapping/saturating alternatives can serve numeric code without weakening defaults. Cost: API surface and exact width semantics.

title: Indexing outside an array or a missing map key fails at runtime; use get for Option.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Keep safe bounds/key checks; keep get and potentially add checked place-update APIs.

title: Parser resource caps: 256 bracket levels, 256 consecutive unary operators, 1000 AST depth.
section: Execution, host boundaries, and resource limits
relax: Keep graceful errors; permit configured compiler budgets or iterative parsing where practical. Cost: resource predictability/implementation effort.
